name: Rare Artifacts
lines: The Orrery of Nine Hours
a paving slab that rocks underfoot
This one slab rocks when you step on it, and the grit round its edges has been scraped clean by a fingernail.
Under the slab, wrapped in oilcloth, something small and brass is ticking.
A brass model of a sky that never was: one sun, nine small worlds on their own rings, all turning to a clock with nine hours in its day. Its maker swore that one day the real sky would agree with it.
A clockmaker's apprentice says her master buried his finest work under the pavement of Somnucor, "where the slabs don't sit flat".
The Silent Bell of Somnucor
a stone with a groove worn round it
Round this stone runs a groove, worn smooth, as though a rope was tied about it for many years.
Roll the stone aside
In the hollow under the stone lies a small bronze bell. You shake it. It makes no sound at all.

The bell from the city's first tower. On the night the city was founded it was rung once, and the sound went out and never came back. It has been silent since. Some say it is still ringing, somewhere else.
The lamp-keepers of Stillspire say the bell that rang once and never again drifted here, where nothing makes a sound: "under a roped stone, out on the Shardfields".
The Quill of the Last Letter
a stump with a split in it
There is a narrow split down the middle of this old stump, and something pale is wedged deep inside.
Work it out of the split
Out of the split comes a long white quill, its nib still dark with ink that has never dried.
A white quill whose ink never dries. It wrote one letter, the last letter of a long correspondence, and the letter was never sent. Whoever holds it is said to always find the right words, once.
At GiGi's Lounge they say a guest who never checked out left a quill that wrote a letter nobody posted, "pushed into a split stump, well away from the music".
The Compass of Forgotten Things
a mossy stone with a scratched arrow
Someone has scratched a small arrow into this mossy stone. It points straight down.
Dig where the arrow points
A hand's depth down you find a little compass. Its needle does not point north. It swings, slowly, toward something you had forgotten.
A child's brass compass whose needle never points north. It points to whatever you have forgotten: a promise, a name, the way home. The children who found it first used it to remember their mothers.
Ondren children say a compass that points to forgotten things fell through from another world, "under a mossy stone with an arrow scratched on it, out past the spiral gardens".
The Thimble of Small Brave Things
a floorboard with a tiny door painted on it
One floorboard here is a shade darker than the rest, and someone has painted a door no bigger than your thumb on it, green, very nearly worn away.
Lift the floorboard
Under the board, on a scrap of old lace, sits a silver thimble with a crown of points round its rim.

A silver thimble crowned with seven little points. It was given as a kiss by someone who didn't know what a kiss was, and it has made its keepers brave in small ways ever since: the first word, the first step, the first time back.
The planners at the Everbloom Wedding House tell of a thimble given as a kiss and lost. "It's under a floorboard with a door the size of your thumb painted on it," they say, and won't say which room.
The Mariner's Glass Heart
a sea-washed stone that doesn't belong
This stone is round and smooth from the sea, yet it lies far above the tide line. Someone carried it here.
Turn the stone over
Bedded in the sand under the stone is a bottle shaped like a heart. Inside it, a tiny sea rolls quietly back and forth.
A heart of blue glass with a little calm sea inside, made by a sailor for the one waiting at home. Hold it in a storm and your own sea goes calm. He never came back for it.
Sailors on the Endless Sea tell of a glass heart with the sea inside it, left on the witch's island "under a stone the sea never touched".
The Sextant of Unnamed Stars
a little cairn of three stones
Three flat stones are stacked here, the top one turned so its point aims at one particular patch of sky.
Under the bottom stone, in a fold of sailcloth, lies a sextant. Its arc is marked with stars no chart has a name for.

A navigator's sextant whose arc is engraved with stars nobody has named. It always finds the way, even under cloud, even in a dream. Its last owner sailed by it off the edge of every map and came back.
Saphirel's harbour pilots say a navigator left his sextant "under a cairn that points at a star", out beyond the far tunnel.
The Crown of Seven Quiet Kings
a block of stone with a crown cut faintly in it
A crown has been cut into this block, so faintly you only see it when your lamp is low. The block sits on rollers.
Roll the block aside
Under the block, in a stone box lined with velvet gone grey, lies a crown with seven points. It is lighter than it looks.

The crown of seven dwarf-kings who each ruled without once raising their voice. Each added a point to it. The eighth would not wear it, and hid it so that the next king would have to be quiet enough to find it.
Halcyra's palace guards say the Quiet Crown came up from the deep and was hidden again "under a block cut with a crown, high above the avenue".
The Spindle of the Deep Weaver
a stone wrapped in fine grey thread
Fine grey thread is wound round and round this stone, so fine you only see it when it catches your light.
The thread leads under the stone, to a silver spindle still wound with violet yarn that is warm to the touch.
The spindle of the first weaver of the deep, who spun the dark elves' banners from cave-silk. Its yarn never runs out. Whatever is woven with it can never be torn.
Celadine's weavers say the first spindle of the deep was carried here and hidden "under a stone she wrapped in thread, in the far district".
The Snowglobe of Every Winter
a snow drift with a hollow under it
This drift sounds hollow when you tap it. The snow on top is a different white from the snow around it.
Dig into the drift
Inside the drift is a hollow, and in the hollow a snowglobe in which it is gently snowing, all by itself.

A snowglobe that has every winter in it: shake it and it snows on a little town as it snowed on one winter night, any winter you remember. The toymakers of the Pole made it for one child and could never make another.
The toymakers of Isvarden say their finest snowglobe was lost "in a drift that was never snowed on, out at the far edge".
The Music Box of the First Carol
a pine stump with a brass key in the bark
Half grown over by the bark of this pine stump is the bow of a small brass key.
Something under the stump begins to play. You dig, and find a music box of dark wood playing a tune you almost know.
A music box that plays the first carol ever sung, a tune nobody has written down. Everyone who hears it says they knew it as a child.
In Lanternhome they hum a tune nobody can finish. "The box that plays it is under a stump with a key in it," the lamp-keepers say, "beyond the palace".
a stump ringed with tiny mushrooms
A perfect ring of tiny white mushrooms grows round this stump, and in the middle the wood has been hollowed by something patient.
Reach into the hollow
In the hollow, cupped in old leaves, is an acorn of gold, heavy and warm.
The acorn of the first oak, before there were any other trees. It is gold all through. The farmers of the Greenwold say that if it is ever planted, a forest will grow in a night.
Glimmerwold's gardeners talk of a golden acorn "in a stump inside a ring of mushrooms, behind the palace terraces".
The Shepherd's Horn of Seven Valleys
a shepherd's cairn
A shepherd's cairn, the kind that marks a path in fog. One stone near the bottom has been pulled out and put back many times.
Pull out the loose stone
Behind the loose stone is a hollow, and in it a curled ivory horn bound with gold.
A curled horn that can be heard in seven valleys at once. Every lost sheep, every lost child, every lost traveller who hears it finds their way to it.
"A horn you can hear in seven valleys," the water-finders of Wellspring say. "In a cairn, if you can find the one stone that moves."
The Laughing Mask of the First Masquerade
a slab with confetti trodden into it
Old confetti is trodden into the cracks round this one slab, though nobody dances here.
Under the slab, in a box of crushed velvet, lies a mask of gold that seems to be smiling at a joke you nearly understand.
The mask worn by the host of the very first masquerade, the night the Party Planet was named. Whoever wears it can make anyone laugh, once a night.
Jubilee's oldest dancers say the first host's mask was hidden "under a slab where the confetti never got swept".
The Astronomer's Inkwell
a stone with no dust on it
Every stone here wears a coat of dust. This one is clean, as if someone wiped it with a sleeve.
Under the stone, sealed in a small case, is an inkwell of dark glass. The ink inside is the black of the sky above you, with tiny stars in it.
An inkwell filled with the night itself. An astronomer used it to draw the first map of the sky, and every star she drew in it is still there, moving slowly.
Celestara's astronomers say an inkwell full of night was hidden "under the one clean stone, out where the far district starts".
The Chalice of the Quiet Sea
a flat stone set like a lid
This flat stone sits too neatly, like a lid on a pot. There is a fingertip-wide gap at one edge.
Under it is a little vault cut in the rock, and in it a silver chalice holding perfectly still water that does not freeze or boil.
A silver chalice whose water never spills, freezes or boils away. It was left by the first dreamer who walked the drowned streets, as a toast to all who came after.
Coralmere's divers say a silver chalice of still water was set down "under a stone that sits like a lid, as far from the gate as the city reaches".
The Rust Queen's Signet
a deck plate with a ring pressed into it
One deck plate here sits a little proud of the rest, and a ring-shaped mark is pressed into its corner.
Lift the deck plate
Under the plate, wedged among the cables, is a ring of red gold with a seal cut into its face: a crown above a wheel.
The seal ring of the Rust Queen, who ruled the red plains in a story the miners tell. Any letter sealed with it is believed, whoever sends it.
Dockers on the Ares Gateway say the Rust Queen's ring came up from Mars in a crate of ore and was hidden aboard, "under a deck plate with a ring pressed into it".
The Clockmaker's Last Gear
a stone with a tooth-shaped notch
There is a neat notch in this stone, exactly the shape of a gear tooth.
Fit your fingers in the notch and pull
The stone tips back. Under it, bright and unrusted, lies a single brass gear that is slowly turning on its own.
The last gear of a great clock that kept time for a whole world. The clock was lost; the gear kept turning. It has never once stopped.
"There's a gear that turns by itself," the kiln-masters of Kilnhaven say, "under a stone notched like a tooth, past the tunnel."
The Hourglass That Runs Upward
a stone sitting in its own shadow
Odd: this stone casts a shadow toward the Sun, not away from it.
Under the stone lies an hourglass. The sand in it is running up.
An hourglass whose sand runs upward. Nobody knows whether it is counting time back or saving it. Those who keep it say they never feel hurried.
Sahmira's caravan masters say an hourglass runs backward "under a stone whose shadow points the wrong way, at the far end of everything".
The Locket of Unsaid Words
a slab scratched with two letters
Two letters are scratched into this slab, and between them a small heart. The scratches are old.
Under the slab is a locket of gold on a fine chain. It is shut, and warm, as though someone has only just let go of it.
A locket that holds the words someone meant to say and never did. Open it and you hear them, softly, in their voice. Nobody has ever opened it twice.
Someone left a locket in Hearthdeep "under a slab with two letters and a heart", the hearth-tenders say, "and never came back to say it".
a stone wrapped in purple cloth
You can just make out a corner of purple cloth peeping out from under this stone.
Pull out the cloth
The cloth is a veil, and wrapped in it is a hand mirror. In it you see yourself as you would like to be.
A silver hand mirror that shows you as you would most like to be. Its owners always kept it veiled, so as not to forget the face they had.
"There's a mirror in Gemelline that tells you what you wish," a twin says, "under a stone with a purple veil, up by the palace." Her sister says the opposite.
The Map of Nowhere
a cairn of pale stones
Three pale stones, stacked. On the middle one someone has drawn, very small, a compass rose with no north.
Take the stones down
Under the cairn, rolled tight and dry, is a map. As you unroll it, its coastlines quietly redraw themselves.
A map that redraws itself to show wherever you are not. Its last owner used it to find the one place nobody had been, and left it there for the next one.
Pyreline's pit crews say a map that draws itself is hidden far out past the circuits, "under a cairn with a compass that has no north".
The Veyari Song Shell
a stone that hums when you lean on it
Lean on this stone and it hums, very low, one long note.
Beneath it lies a spiral shell of rose and pearl. Hold it to your ear: it is singing the first word of the Veyari language.
A spiral shell that sings the first word the Veyari ever spoke. They say whoever learns to sing it back will understand every language there is.
A trader in Brightwater swears a Veyari elder gave the first word, sealed in a shell, to the future: "under a stone that hums, beyond the palace".
The Tilted Astrolabe
a deck plate set at a slant
This deck plate was fitted at a slant, tilted toward the great window, by someone who wanted it just so.
Under it, in a nest of crystal sand, lies a brass astrolabe tilted at an angle no world's sky has.
This is where you found
